description:
NOVA-X Mission Control 🚀

Design your own space mission to the Moon or Mars! Choose your spacecraft, manage resources, plan trajectories, and make decisions that determine mission success. Our AI-powered Mission Advisor helps you optimize designs, identify risks, and make smarter choices, while our simulation engine puts every decision to the test.

No magic buttons, no guaranteed success — just smart engineering and space adventure!

6 Minds. One Mission. Zero Room for Bad Calculations. 🌌

details:
Mission Forge — Fused Edition
Mission Forge is a space mission design game. Define a science objective, build a spacecraft, select an orbit and launcher, then fly the mission and review the debrief. It supports solo play, hot-seat teams, and online rooms for up to four players.

The fused edition includes mission and instrument references, saved design comparison, a first-mission guide, the full How to use tutorial, a guided tab tour, and decision-specific debriefs. Every instrument’s ? button opens a centered, text-only details panel. Instrument cards add or remove payload; instruments can also be dragged to payload slots. Orbit choices use a path diagram because an orbit is not a physical component. Estimates are simplified game values and are labeled as such.

The How to use button explains controls, design tabs, team seats, flight playback, and spacecraft tradeoffs. Tab tour explains each design tab and returns to the tab you started on. Flight playback can be paused, replayed, stepped, sped up, or scrubbed with the keyboard. Screen-reader announcements follow the selected point in flight; dialogs support keyboard focus and closing. Reduced-motion settings pause automatic playback.

The interface includes a skip link, visible keyboard focus, and keyboard navigation across design tabs. Saved design names are escaped before display, and storage errors are reported when a design cannot be saved.

Mission and flight features
Define your mission: choose a body, science objective, priority, and adjustable requirements for life, data return, budget, orbit, and science. Objective instruments receive full science weight; unrelated instruments receive reduced weight.
Requirements and debrief: each requirement has a difficulty weight that affects the score multiplier. Failed requirements explain the spacecraft or mission choice that caused them. Preset missions also include science-target checks and stronger life and data thresholds.
Mission types: orbiters use a monthly operating mission. The Comet Dust Flyby has no orbit insertion, observes for a short encounter, and challenges the onboard buffer, compression, and downlink.
Live simulation: the flight advances in daily steps, tracking battery charge, propellant, onboard data, panel degradation, instrument load shedding, and downlink. The report plots these values and includes a zoomed orbit-power view.
Spacecraft view: a generated SVG reflects the selected bus, panels, radio, instruments, attitude control, propulsion, propellant, and launcher fairing. Panels deploy during flight; orbiters show an insertion burn.
Team play: hot-seat roles own parts of the design and have role goals. Online rooms synchronize one shared design, enforce seat ownership and resource allowances, record trade requests and Ready-vote churn, and launch one shared seeded flight. Solo scoring uses decision quality instead of granting team coordination points.
Leaderboards and sharing: design codes include custom mission settings. The optional server leaderboard recalculates submitted flights and separates preset boards by scenario, difficulty, and crew size. Custom boards also separate exact requirement settings. Challenge codes create a board for the same design and seed.
Balance checks: the automated search samples designs at each difficulty and checks default mission pressure and variety among high-scoring architectures.
